item.title: A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.04690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension. The same equality holds for every specialization-closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ when $B$ is a finite-type algebra over a noetherian domain $A$ of finite character and either $A$ or $B$ is regular. These equalities classify the thick Hom-submodules closed under existing coproducts. We also prove the corresponding bounded-above statement from the support results of Matsui--Takahashi. For an arbitrary noetherian ring, the bounded-below generation conjecture reduces to torsion complexes over quotient domains, with their support unchanged. Finally, over a regular noetherian domain of infinite dimension, we give a bounded-below object which is generated by bounded objects with the same support but has no bounded-below representative by finitely generated modules. The comparison functor from the bounded-below derived category of finite modules is therefore neither full nor essentially surjective.
item.dc:creator: Liangyu Zhu

item.title: Coherence and the Hilbert-syzygy identity for power series over valuation domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.05246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a complete valuation domain of rank 1, and let $\Gamma$ be its value group. We investigate the power series ring $V[[t]]$, and finally answer the long standing question of when this ring is coherent. Specifically, we prove that it is coherent if and only if $V$ is almost maximal, and either $\Gamma = \mathbb{R}$ or $\Gamma$ is discrete. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the weak Hilbert-syzygy identity $w. dim V [[X]] = w. dim V + 1$ holds if and only if $V[[X]]$ is a coherent ring.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui, Adam Jones, Yiding Wang

item.title: Geometry of Spaces of Subrings
item.description: arXiv:2611.05370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by examples such as the local rings of projective integral schemes and the Zariski-Riemann space of a field, we develop a geometry for continuously indexed families of subrings of a commutative ring $R$. The indexing spaces are Stone spaces, and continuity is taken with respect to the Zariski topology on the space of subrings. To each such family we associate a subsheaf of the constant sheaf with value $R$ whose stalks are the indexed subrings. This gives a patch ringed space. Its global sections are locally constant $R$-valued functions whose value at each point belongs to the corresponding subring. The ring of global sections, with this representation, is the associated patch algebra. Our main result establishes an algebra-geometry correspondence between these continuously indexed families of subrings and patch ringed spaces that can be expressed as a category equivalence, with each of the two categories dually equivalent to the category of patch algebras. Thus the indexing space, its sheaf, and the indexed subrings can be recovered functorially from the associated patch algebra, which serves as a coordinate ring for this geometry. We describe kernels and factorizations of patch algebra morphisms in geometric terms and characterize their injectivity and surjectivity. We include applications to Pierce duality and Bhatt-Scholze $w$-localizations of integral separated quasi-compact schemes.
item.dc:creator: Laura Cossu, Bruce Olberding, Giovanni Secreti

item.title: Localisations of rings of weak global dimension at most one
item.description: arXiv:2611.05247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterise the commutative rings of weak global dimension at most one whose derived categories can be stratified by the Balmer-Favi support theory. For such rings, this yields a bijective correspondence between the class of localising subcategories of the derived category, and the subsets of the Zariski spectrum. For a large class of rings of weak global dimension at most one including all valuation domains, this occurs if and only if the ring is locally strongly discrete, if and only if the Telescope conjecture holds, and if and only if the module category has Gabriel dimension. However, we also give an example of a valuation domain where all these conditions fail, and yet the residue fields generate its derived category and we can classify all the localising subcategories of $D(R)$. Additionally, in the same example, we show that the Balchin-Stevenson smashing support cannot stratify $D(R)$ either.
item.dc:creator: Jan \v{S}\v{t}ov\'i\v{c}ek, Florian Tecklenburg

item.title: The tensor triangular geometry of valuation domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.05298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the tensor triangular geometry of derived categories of valuation domains, obtaining complete ring-theoretic characterizations of their main structural properties. In particular, although valuation domains are almost always non-noetherian, their derived categories always satisfy the local-to-global principle and hence the detection property. We establish precise criteria for homological detection, stratification, and homological stratification, revealing a clear hierarchy among these properties. Notably, we obtain examples of derived categories of commutative rings that are homologically stratified and satisfy the local-to-global principle, but are not stratified. We also determine when the category of modules over a valuation domain has Gabriel dimension, and use this to provide a negative answer to a question of Balchin, G\'omez and Stevenson. Overall, valuation domains provide a rich class of non-noetherian rings whose derived categories can be understood in considerable depth.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Barthel, Drew Heard, Beren Sanders, Changhan Zou

item.title: Homology with the theme of Matlis
item.description: arXiv:2212.10332v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Matlis proved a lot of homological properties of the fraction field of an integral domain. In this paper, we simplify and extend some of them from 1-dimensional (resp. rank one) cases to the higher dimensional (resp. finite rank) cases. For example, we study the weakly co-torsion property of Ext$(-,\sim)$, and use it to present splitting criteria. These are equipped with several applications. For instance, we compute the projective dimension of $\widehat{R}$ and present some non-noetherian versions of Grothendieck's localization problem. We construct a new class of co-Hopfian modules and extend Matlis' decomposability problem to higher ranks. In particular, this paper deals with the basic properties of Matlis' quadric $(Q,Q/R, \widehat{R},\overset{\sim}R).$
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Elham Mahdavi

item.title: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2503.15037v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,\Sigma_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $\Sigma_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(\Sigma)$. Inspired by the work of Shen--Sun--Weng, we introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}^d(\Sigma)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(\Sigma)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$ other than $\Sigma_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(\Sigma_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: On Shilov boundaries, Rees valuations and integral extensions
item.description: arXiv:2507.07091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore an analogy between, on one hand, the notions of integral closure of ideals and Rees valuations in commutative algebra and, on the other hand, the notions of spectral seminorm and Shilov boundary in nonarchimedean geometry. For any Tate ring $\mathcal{A}$ with a Noetherian ring of definition $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and pseudo-uniformizer $\varpi\in\mathcal{A}_{0}$, we prove that the Shilov boundary for $\mathcal{A}$ naturally coincides with the set of Rees valuation rings of the principal ideal $(\varpi)_{\mathcal{A}_{0}}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{0}$. Furthermore, we characterize the Shilov boundary for a wide class of Tate rings by means of minimal open prime ideals in the subring of power-bounded elements. For affinoid algebras, in the sense of Tate, whose underlying rings are integral domains, this recovers a well-known result of Berkovich. Moreover, under some mild assumptions, we prove stability of our characterization of the Shilov boundary under (completed) integral extensions. In particular, for every mixed-characteristic Noetherian domain $R$, we obtain a description of the Shilov boundary for the Tate ring $\widehat{R^{+}}[p^{-1}]$, where $\widehat{R^{+}}$ is the $p$-adic completion of the absolute integral closure of the domain $R$.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: Descent along flat composed with radicalization
item.description: arXiv:2609.24577v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the following general situation. Let $R\to S$ be a finite flat morphism of regular rings of zero (resp. prime) mixed or (equi)-characteristic. For $P\in Spec R$, put $A=R/P, C=S/PS,$ and $B=S/\sqrt{PS}=C_{\mathrm{red}}.$ The basic question is whether a property of $B$ forces the same property of $A$. The main point is that ordinary finite-flat descent applies naturally to $A\to C$, whereas the passage $C\to C_{\mathrm{red}}$ may (not) destroy nilpotent information.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: When Hilbert functions determine generic initial ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.07799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we characterize the Hilbert functions that determine the degree reverse lexicographic generic initial ideal among Artinian quotients of embedding dimension $n\ge2$ with the $(n-2)$-strong Lefschetz property. The criterion is a finite arithmetic test on successive positive differences of the Hilbert function. It uses recursively defined integer vectors and requires no construction of a monomial ideal. When uniqueness holds, the same vectors recover the common generic initial ideal degree by degree. The proof reduces uniqueness successively to uniqueness of lower sets of specified cardinalities in Borel orders. In four variables, the test simplifies to avoidance of explicitly computed integer intervals. We recover the quasi-symmetry criterion of Harima and Wachi and give infinite families beyond that criterion in every number of variables at least four.
item.dc:creator: Van Duc Trung

item.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
item.description: arXiv:2512.18654v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.
item.dc:creator: Rahim Rahmati-Asghar

item.title: Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes
item.description: arXiv:2605.14803v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex, which can be considered as a derived variant of the module of Frobenius--Witt differentials defined by T. Saito. This new object also can be seen as an arithmetic variant of the notion of cotangent complex. We explain the suitability of these two viewpoints through a series of propositions. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes and the regularity of noetherian local rings, which can be considered as a derived variant of Saito's regularity criterion. This proof relies heavily on computations of Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes in the case of perfectoid rings. We also study the deformation theory of delta structures using Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes.
item.dc:creator: Kanau Shimada

item.title: A note on prismatic sites for p-quasisyntomic rings
item.description: arXiv:2607.04931v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a fixed prime number and let $R$ be a $p$-quasisyntomic ring. We provide conditions for objects in the absolute prismatic site $R_\Prism$ to cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and to admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$. More precisely, we introduce in $R_\Prism$ the so-called transversal objects, so that the coproduct of any object in $R_\Prism$ with a transversal object exists in $R_\Prism$. As an immediate generalization, we introduce the so-called relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid covers of $R$, whose prismatic cohomology (of $\delta$-pairs, in the sense of Antieau-Krause-Nikolaus) produces objects in $R_\Prism$ that cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$.
item.dc:creator: Jingbang Guo
